narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the story; reads all narration and genealogies.

joseph-the-patriarch.name: Joseph
joseph-the-patriarch.note: Jacob's favoured son; candid dreamer at seventeen, then upright slave and calm interpreter of dreams in prison.

butler-and-baker.name: The butler and the baker
butler-and-baker.note: Pharao's two imprisoned officers answering together, downcast.

chief-butler.name: Chief butler
chief-butler.note: Pharao's cupbearer in prison, recounting his dream hopefully.

chief-baker.name: Chief baker
chief-baker.note: Pharao's baker in prison, encouraged by the butler's good omen as he tells his dream.

1.t: After this, it came to pass, that two eunuchs, the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, offended their lord.

2.t: And Pharao being angry with them, (now the one was chief butler, the other chief baker,)

3.t: He sent them to the prison of the commander of the soldiers, in which Joseph also was prisoner.

4.t: But the keeper of the prison delivered them to Joseph, and he served them. Some little time passed, and they were kept in custody.

5.t: And they both dreamed a dream the same night, according to the interpretation agreeing to themselves:

6.t: And when Joseph was come into them in the morning, and saw them sad,

7.t: Why is your countenance sadder today than usual?

8.t: We have dreamed a dream, and there is nobody to interpret it to us.
Doth not interpretation belong to God? Tell me what you have dreamed:

9.t: The chief butler first told his dream:
I saw before me a vine,

10.t: On which were three branches, which by little and little sent out buds, and after the blossoms brought forth ripe grapes:

11.t: And the cup of Pharao was in my hand: and I took the grapes, and pressed them into the cup which I held, and I gave the cup to Pharao.

12.t: This is the interpretation of the dream: The three branches, are yet three days:

13.t: After which Pharao will remember thy service, and will restore thee to thy former place: and thou shalt present him the cup according to thy office, as before thou was wont to do.

14.t: Only remember me when it shall be well with thee, and do me this kindness: to put Pharao in mind to take me out of this prison:

15.t: For I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews, and here without any fault was cast into the dungeon.

16.t: The chief baker seeing that he had wisely interpreted the dream, said:
I also dreamed a dream, That I had three baskets of meal upon my head:

17.t: And that in one basket which was uppermost, I carried all meats that are made by the art of baking, and that the birds ate out of it.

18.t: This is the interpretation of the dream: The three baskets, are yet three days:

19.t: After which Pharao will take thy head from thee, and hang thee on a cross, and the birds shall tear thy flesh.

20.t: The third day after this was the birthday of Pharao: and he made a great feast for his servants, and at the banquet remembered the chief butler, and the chief baker.

21.t: And he restored the one to his place, to present him the cup:

22.t: The other he hanged on a gibbet, that the truth of the interpreter might be shewn.

23.t: But the chief butler, when things prospered with him, forgot his interpreter.
